tone_statements.citation: [Reviewer not seen]. 2014. Review of: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation (Trends in Linguistics Studies and Monographs 229, De Gruyter Mouton). SIL Electronic Book Reviews 2014-003. Dallas: SIL International.
tone_statements.quote: Helpho and Phuza have a four-tone system, while Muji, Phola, and Azha have a five-tone system. For each of the tone systems, JP provides F0 pitch plot graphs in nasal and stop initial environments. All of the languages, except Azha, have tone sandhi rules. For all the languages contour tones are only a phonetic phenomenon. … JP does mention when there is noticeable phonetic occurrence of phonation, e.g., creaky voice for Phuza’s low rising toneme, tense voice for /21/ and /13/ tonemes in Hlepho, etc.
tone_statements.locator: section 'Phula phonologies: Five representative sketches', 8th page of the unpaginated review; summarises Pelkey 2011 ch. 5
tone_statements.summary: Four tonemes, reported second-hand from Pelkey 2011; only /21/ and /13/ are named here (often tense-voiced); contour tones said to be phonetic only; tone sandhi present. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2022. The phonetic tone change *high > rising: Evidence from the Ngwi dialect laboratory. Diachronica 39(2): 226-267. Amsterdam: John Benjamins. (Accompanying open CLDF dataset: lexibank/yangyi, ed. J.-M. List, CC-BY-4.0, in which 'Hlepho Phowa [yhl]' = language 74, source Pelkey2011, 693 tone-marked forms.)

sources.note: Examines tone-change pathways to rising tones in Ngwi; 'among the 11 Ngwi language clusters examined, a new rising tone value has unambiguously developed from an historically high tone in nine of them'; for Hlepho it would give the modern reflex values (e.g. low-rising 13) of Proto-Ngwi tone classes, not a synchronic description of the tone system; article not opened (paywalled).
